# `response-header-became-optional`

Response header became optional

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `response-header-became-optional` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Responses ([RULES.md section 6](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A required response header is now optional.

## Why this default

Clients may assume it is always present and fail when it is missing.

## Example

From test case [`response-header-became-optional`](../../test/cases/response-header-became-optional/): Required → optional.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
            headers:
              X-Request-Id:
-               required: true
                schema:
                  type: string
```

Findings:

- `response-header-became-optional` · error · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  response-header-became-optional: error
```

## How to fix

Keep it required, or make sure clients check for it first.
